audit.recode_to: If Österberg 1914 (or another primary) states it: fixed root-/first-syllable main stress of the Swedish type (quantity-insensitive, lexical accent 1/2 + central-Jämtland two-peaked circumflex as tonal overlay; East-Jämtland compound-final stress kept as a sub-dialectal morphology note). Do not reclassify by presumption before a primary statement is in hand.

A a full-text search for stress/accent Westin (89 pp) confirms there is no simplex stress-placement statement elsewhere in it. sources.note: History of the Trøndelag (Norway) dialects: monosyllabic, disyllabic and circumflex tonal accents (pp. 39-40, after Reitan 1922) described for trøndersk. Jamtska only mentioned: shared apocope (p. 38), two-peaked circumflex on apocopated words (p. 39). 165 of 442 pp. seen; no Jämtland system there.

tone.quote: Dei forkorta tostavingsorda har, sjølv om dei no er einstava, eit eige tonelag, eit såkalla cirkumflekstonelag, som i lydskrift kan markeras ved cirkumfleksaksenten /^/: /krŷ:p/, /må̂:n/, /sû:p/. Det kan høras ut som vokalen blir gjentatt i slike ord: /kry:yp/, /må:ån/, /su:up/, og det vart tidlegare også kalla "totoppa staving". Denne nemninga høver for den uttalen som apokoperte ord har i jemtsk, men i den trønderske cirkumfleksen er det ikkje så tydeleg gjentaking av vokalen. Her er det tonen som er det viktigaste.
tone.translation: The shortened disyllabic words have, even though they are now monosyllabic, a tonal accent of their own, a so-called circumflex accent, which in phonetic script can be marked with the circumflex sign /^/: /krŷ:p/, /må̂:n/, /sû:p/. It can sound as if the vowel is repeated in such words: /kry:yp/, /må:ån/, /su:up/, and it was earlier also called 'two-peaked syllable'. This term suits the pronunciation that apocopated words have in Jämtland dialect (jemtsk), but in the Trøndelag circumflex there is no such clear repetition of the vowel. Here it is the tone that matters most.

sources.note: On apocope and the two-peaked (circumflex) accent in Trøndelag/Nordmøre dialects; presupposes single vs double 'tonelag' (accent 1/2), declines to describe the musical accent (defers to Storm, p. 75). tone.translation: The double toneme is preserved in Lierne² and Nordmøre except Rindal and the northernmost( districts ... In Lierne and southern Nordmøre one thus says e̥ı vîs, whereas elsewhere in Trøndelag it is vı̌s or vīs ... ² So also Jämtland, Geijer Tilljämning ock apokope p. 16. ... [p. 55:] Cf. Jessen's account of the two-peaked accentuation in Jämtland p. 8: 'Vowel doubling in Jämtlandic is to be taken literally; e.g. kaast is to be pronounced with 2 a's in the same syllable, i.e. a »diphthong« in the most literal sense'.

Artiklen -en] er svag „Halvlyd“, og kræver „Acutus“ („hög ton“) i Stammen; Ordene ere jét, silld, sènng, samt de med Omlyd som fót, ònnd osv.; ... To andre Masc. have -er, men med „Gravis“ („låg ton“) : vènn, sòn. ... akksel (Skulder -dre; Sing. Acutus, Pl. Gravis) ... STUGUN og RAGUNDA. tone.translation: ... is written here -er, in which e [as in the masc. article -en] is a weak 'half-sound', and requires 'Acutus' ('high tone') in the stem; the words are jét, silld, sènng, and those with umlaut like fót, ònnd etc.; ... Two other masculines have -er, but with 'Gravis' ('low tone'): vènn, sòn. ... akksel (shoulder; sing. Acutus, pl. Gravis) ... STUGUN and RAGUNDA. To the ear very unlike, because of the accent (quick in Stugun, drawling in Ragunda); in written form the difference becomes small.
